name: Methi Murgh
subtitle: chicken braised with fresh fenugreek, bitter-sweet and thick rather than soupy

ingredients.note: thigh and drumstick hold up better than breast
deepens the fenugreek note at the end

prepNotes: Toss the picked methi leaves with 1 tsp salt, leave 20 minutes, then squeeze out the dark liquid hard. This is what stops the dish turning harshly bitter.
Take the yogurt out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead. Cold yogurt splits the moment it hits a hot pan.
Pat the chicken dry so it browns instead of steaming.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the sliced onion over medium heat until evenly golden brown, 12-14 minutes.
steps.tip: Stir every couple of minutes and take it to gold, not mahogany. Burnt onion turns the gravy bitter and there is no rescuing it.

steps.text: Add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes and the oil looks clear at the edges.
Add the chicken and green chillies and sear over high heat 5 minutes, until the pieces are opaque all over.
Lower the heat, stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powders with 2 tbsp water, and fry 3 minutes until the oil separates.
steps.tip: The splash of water keeps the ground spices from scorching in the few seconds before the chicken juices come out.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat for 30 seconds, whisk in the yogurt a spoonful at a time, then return to low heat and cook 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Off the heat and a spoon at a time. This is the only reliable way to keep yogurt from curdling into grains.

steps.text: Fold in the squeezed methi leaves and salt, and cook uncovered 8 minutes, until the leaves collapse and darken.
Cover and simmer on low 12 minutes, stirring twice, until the chicken is tender and the gravy clings to the pieces.
Uncover and cook off any watery liquid over medium heat, 3-4 minutes. Methi murgh should be thick enough to scoop, not ladle.
Sprinkle over the garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, spoon on the ghee, and rest covered 5 minutes off the heat.
Finish with coriander leaves and lemon juice, and serve with rumali roti or plain rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat gently on the stovetop with 2 tbsp water; the microwave dries the chicken out.
